name: West Virginia

agency.name: West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection (WVDEP)

overview: WVDEP's Division of Air Quality issues construction, modification, relocation, and temporary permits under 45CSR13 for stationary sources above the rule's thresholds, plus Class I and Class II general permit registrations (filed through the Electronic Submission System), PSD permits (45CSR14), nonattainment NSR permits (45CSR19), and Title V operating permits (45CSR30). Fees are under 45CSR22. A Permit Determination request confirms whether a permit is needed. West Virginia has extensive oil and gas general permits: G70-E for well sites and G35-E for compressor and dehydration facilities. There are no local air agencies.

permitTypes.name: Permit Determination / below 45CSR13 thresholds
permitTypes.description: Sources below the 45CSR13 stationary source thresholds and not subject to an emission control rule do not need a permit. DAQ will confirm through a Permit Determination (no fee, 30 business days).

permitTypes.name: General Permit Registrations (Class I and Class II)
permitTypes.description: G10-D coal preparation/handling; G20-C hot mix asphalt (minor); G33-A natural gas compressor station spark-ignition engines 25-500 hp (Class I); G35-E natural gas compressor and/or dehydration facilities; G40-C nonmetallic minerals processing; G50-C concrete batch plants (minor); G60-D emergency generators (Class II); G65-D single emergency generator (Class I); G70-E natural gas production at the well site. Class I: no public notice, 45-day review, $250. Class II: 30-day applicant notice, 45-day review, $500 plus 45CSR22 fees.

permitTypes.name: 45CSR13 Construction / Modification Permit
permitTypes.description: Required for new stationary sources and modifications. 30-day DAQ public notice; 90-day review after completeness (extendable 30 days for comments); $1,000 plus 45CSR22 fees (e.g., NSPS, NESHAP/MACT/toxics add-ons). Relocation and temporary permits (6 months, extendable) also available. Class I/II administrative updates handle smaller changes.
permitTypes.quote: six (6) pounds per hour and ten (10) tons per year or 144 pounds/day of VOCs or any regulated air pollutant ... more than two (2) pounds per hour or (5) five tons per year of HAPs on an aggregated basis

permitTypes.name: Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD)
permitTypes.description: New major sources or major modifications in attainment areas. Decision within six months of a complete application.
permitTypes.thresholds: 100 tons/year or more for Table 1 source categories; 250 tons/year or more for other sources; major modification above 45CSR14 significance thresholds (restated from the DAQ Permitting Handbook).

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment NSR
permitTypes.description: Sources with potential to emit 100 tons/year or more in nonattainment areas and major modifications; requires LAER and offsets.

permitTypes.name: Title V Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: Five-year permits; annual fee based on prior-year actual emissions. DAQ has 60 days to determine completeness and 12 months to act on initial or renewal permits.
permitTypes.thresholds: More than 100 tons/year of regulated pollutants; 10 tons/year of a single HAP or 25 tons/year of combined HAPs; sources subject to CAA sections 111 and 112 unless deferred (restated from the DAQ Permitting Handbook).

oilAndGas.summary: West Virginia (Marcellus/Utica) uses general permits for upstream and midstream gas. G70-E covers natural gas production facilities at the well site and replaces G70-A through G70-D (G70-D registrations are automatically covered). G35-E (issued September 5, 2024) covers natural gas compressor and/or dehydration facilities and replaces G30-D and G35-A/C/D. G33-A covers small compressor engines. DAQ's well pad guidance explains when a permit is generally triggered and which NSPS (OOOO/OOOOa/OOOOb) applies by date. Well completion notifications are due at least 2 days before each completion.

programs.name: G70-E: Natural Gas Production Facilities at the Well Site
programs.description: Class II general permit for well sites; annual certification and annual fee. Alternative Operating Scenario notifications are filed through ESS.
programs.thresholds: DAQ guidance: a permit is generally required if condensate production exceeds 0.5 barrels (21 gallons) per day, or facility-wide uncontrolled VOC potential exceeds 6 lb/hr (144 lb/day), or benzene/formaldehyde reaches 1,000 lb/yr or more (restated).

programs.name: G35-E: Natural Gas Compressor and/or Dehydration Facilities
programs.description: General permit issued September 5, 2024 for new registrations and modifications at compressor and dehydration facilities; existing G35-D permits are treated as G35-E.

programs.name: G33-A: Natural Gas Compressor Station Engines
programs.description: Class I general permit for spark-ignition engines of 25 to 500 hp, incorporating NSPS JJJJ.
